attacks.claim: On upstream 429 the gateway retries once after sleeping up to 5s while holding the client request open. Upstream 429s are described as a shared-capacity problem, so every tenant's request retries against the same saturated upstream. That doubles upstream load exactly when it is most constrained, and the held requests and sleeping timers have no concurrency cap or budget. The retry is also not counted against the tenant bucket, so it bypasses the isolation this PR adds.
attacks.evidence: "req.log.warn({ tenant: tenant.id, delay }, \"upstream 429, retrying once\"); await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, delay)); res = await upstream.chat(req.body, { signal: req.signal });" with no global retry budget, concurrency bound, or retry metric in the diff
